draft.title: Rebuttal
card: A rebuttal is part of an argument where the writer deals with an opposing view. The writer first states what the other side says, then answers it.
The answer shows why the opposing view is weak. The writer might point to missing evidence, a flaw in the reasoning, or a cost the other side ignores.

Example: a writer says some people think homework builds good habits. The writer then replies that a student who copies answers only learns to copy. The first step states the other view. The second shows why it is weak.

A rebuttal makes the writer's case stronger. It shows the reader that the writer has thought about the other side and still holds their position. Phrases such as "Some argue" and "However" often signal one.
draft.remember: A rebuttal states the opposing view fairly, then shows why it is weak.

a.q: What is the main job of a rebuttal in a persuasive text?
opts: To answer an opposing view by showing its weakness
To repeat the writer's own view in stronger words
To list facts that all readers already accept
To sum up the whole text in the final paragraph
a.why: A rebuttal deals with the other side by stating it and showing why it is weak. Repeating your own view in stronger words is tempting, but it never engages with the opposing argument, so it is not a rebuttal.
a.clue: Think about whose view the writer is answering.

b.q: Priya argues that her school should start later. First she says some people fear students will just go to bed later. Then she cites sleep studies showing teenagers naturally fall asleep later, so a later start suits them. Which part is the rebuttal?
opts: Both steps together, the opposing view and the answer
Only the first step, which states what some people say
Only the second step, which gives the sleep evidence
Neither step, because her own view is not restated
b.why: A rebuttal has two steps: it states the opposing view and shows why it is weak. Both are needed. The first step alone is only the opposing view, which is tempting to call the rebuttal because it is the part about the other side.
b.clue: A rebuttal needs both the other side and the answer to it.

a.best: To answer an opposing view by showing its weakness

b.best: Both steps together, the opposing view and the answer
